title: Bond Market Swings Affect Your Savings, Investments
summary: Bloomberg's Nikki Waller and David Gura join Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." The Treasury surprised traders this week with its plan to buy back more debt. Long-dated yields plunged on Wednesday in response to the news, only to rebound the next day. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Wild Weather Sends Crop Prices Rising in Risk to China Trade
summary: Extreme weather is trimming US harvests and boosting prices for farmers just as top commodities importer China is increasing soybean purchases to meet a commitment struck between the two nations’ leaders.

title: US Yields Soar, AI Pushback, Playing Politics: Roundtable
summary: Bloomberg's Nikki Waller, Sarah Frier, and David Gura join Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss the whiplash in the US Treasury market this week and how it impacts personal finance and politics. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Hedge Funds Cut Bearish Bets on European Diesel to Two-Year Low
summary: Hedge funds slashed short-only positions on European diesel to the lowest in over two years while stacking up fresh bullish wagers, a sign that traders anticipate that a historic fuels crunch will stretch on.

title: Bessent’s Bond Maneuvers Giving Global Debasement Trade New Life
summary: Scott Bessent’s bid to tame US borrowing costs knocked down long-term yields for barely a day. The more lasting market signal: the dollar weakened while gold and Bitcoin rallied, reinforcing a debasement trade fueled by swelling US deficits and concerns over the direction of US economic policy.

title: US Stocks End Week on Up Note, Nasdaq 100 Snaps Five-Day Slump
summary: US stocks rose on Friday, finishing the week on an upbeat note that saw the Nasdaq 100 end a five-day losing streak as data revealed bustling business activity and Bitcoin soared.

title: Nasdaq 100 Halts Five-Day Slump as Bitcoin Rallies: Markets Wrap
summary: The final stretch of a jittery week on Wall Street saw stocks rising amid solid economic data, with traders weighing the outlook for bonds after a burst of volatility.

title: Binance Faces New Scrutiny in Its Crypto-Friendly UAE Haven
summary: Police inquiries involving Binance Holdings Ltd. employees in the United Arab Emirates are testing the crypto exchange in a country that has become one of its most important bases, after investigators scrutinized a bank account it uses to hold customer money.

title: Week of Whiplash in Treasuries Is Closing With Muddied Outlook
summary: After a turbulent stretch for the US bond market, traders are heading into the weekend with questions about what Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s next move will be.

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 21
summary: Oil capped a weekly gain as traders awaited details of a US campaign to isolate Iran’s economy, with no apparent end in sight to a conflict that has slashed Middle East exports.

title: US Natural Gas Rises on Intensifying Heat, Texas Power Forecasts
summary: US natural gas futures ended higher as forecasts shifted to show hotter weather in the coming weeks, indicating higher demand for gas-fired power as consumers ramp up their air-conditioning use.

title: US Chief Justice Lets Trump Keep Building Ballroom for Now
summary: US Chief Justice John Roberts said President Donald Trump can keep building his new White House ballroom for now while the Supreme Court considers issuing a longer-term order blessing continued construction of the massive structure. Bloomberg's June Grasso joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Clock Ticks Down on New Canada Tariff Deadline
summary: Sarah Bianchi, senior managing director at Evercore ISI and former deputy US trade representative, joined Balance of Power to discuss the upcoming tariff deadline. Bianchi said that after the US strikes a tariff deal with Canada, Mexico will likely ask for similar relief.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Allspring’s Miletti Sees Jackson Hole as Bigger Risk Than Nvidia
summary: Allspring Global Investments’ Ann Miletti said Wall Street has more to worry about from next week’s Jackson Hole economic symposium than earnings from AI bellwether Nvidia Corp.

title: Mexican Governor Accused by US of Cartel Ties Returns to His Job
summary: The Mexican governor accused by the US of conspiring with a major criminal cartel to traffic drugs is ending his leave of absence, pledging to finish out his term through next year in a move that could inflame tensions with Washington.

title: SEC Accuses Ex-BofA Senior Banker Satsky of Insider Trading
summary: Former senior Bank of America Corp. investment banker Jason Satsky was accused by the US Securities and Exchange Commission of providing an insider-trading tip to a friend who allegedly made $18.5 million in illegal profits.

title: China’s Traders Find Meaning in ‘Niu Lai’
summary: A crude animated film has become a meme for Chinese retail investors who see their own market struggles in its characters. Bloomberg Opinion columnist Shuli Ren explains why “Niu Lai” has struck a nerve. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Jackson Hole a Bigger Market Risk Than Nvidia for Allspring’s Miletti
summary: Ann Miletti, head of equity investments and chief diversity officer at Allspring Global Investments, says she is keeping expectations low heading into the Jackson Hole Symposium and sees it posing a greater near-term market risk than Nvidia earnings. She speaks with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Anthropic Investor Slams VC’s AI Miss | Open Interest 8/21/2026
summary: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." AI spending hits overdrive as Broadcom eyes a massive $60 billion debt deal ahead of Nvidia earnings. Anthropic sets its sights on a potentially record-breaking IPO. Early Anthropic investor Anjney Midha unloads on traditional venture capital, arguing firms failed investors by missing the AI revolution. Plus, Critical Metals CEO Tony Sage says his company's key Greenland mining project is on track. (Source: Bloomberg)
